findings.title: A drill-down the model drops on a re-run is lost, and then its SVG is deleted
quotes: On a re-run keep the old source and images lines and every `## Drill-down: ` section below the diagrams, unchanged (FR-25).
and that this run will not draw: no current diagram section's name (step 4) and no image a `## Drill-down: ` section links

findings.fix: before the skill rewrites explainer.md, have `finish` (or a new step) record the drill-down headings. Have `finish` refuse, writing nothing and deleting nothing, when a previously recorded drill-down heading is missing. Add an integration test: an explainer whose drill-down was removed after a first `finish`; a second `finish` exits 1 and the drill-down's SVG is byte-unchanged.

sources.situation: on a re-run, the model rewrites explainer.md and leaves out a `## Drill-down:` section. The human drove that drill-down interactively, and the text is now gone with no copy. Then `nio explain finish` runs step 3. No section links the drill-down's image any more and no current section has its name, but the old images line still lists it, so the SVG is deleted. If it was never committed, it cannot be recovered. TC-9 is e2e and only proves the case where the model keeps the section.

findings.reason: CT-5 step 3 deletes a listed SVG when no current section or drill-down link names it, and step 4/5 list drill-down images; a drill-down section the model drops leaves its SVG deletable, and only the skill text (not finish) guards the section; TC-9 covers only the kept case.
findings.note: Human Q15: finish records drill-down headings and refuses before writing or deleting if one is missing (CT-5, TC-43)

sources.situation: the plan changes and `nio status` flags the explainer as stale. Someone runs `nio explain finish`, as TC-29 and QS-4 step 2 do. Nothing records the drift any more (only the drill-down marker hints at it), and a developer now trusts an explainer the plan has outgrown. This is the misuse UJ-1 names.

findings.title: An older nio reads the "Read first" line as an edit to the approved plan
quotes: makes `Read first: [explainer.md](explainer.md)` the first line of quickstart.md's body, once
`flow.judged_blob` and `flow.scan` compare quickstart.md through `planned` as they do tasks.md.
findings.fix: state the minimum nio version for an effort whose quickstart carries the line, for example by having `finish` refuse unless the flow state was written by a nio that knows CT-9. Or say plainly in the plan that a mixed-version team must upgrade first, and add a test showing that removing the line by hand restores a byte-identical quickstart (the way back).

sources.situation: one clone, with the new nio, runs `@nio:explain` and commits quickstart.md with the line. Another clone still has the old nio. Its `flow.scan` compares quickstart.md by its raw `hash-object`, sees a plan-gate file edited after approval, and sends the effort back to `plan_jury` with a `back` line. That line goes into the append-only history, which only `nio flow` writes and no one can retract by hand. FR-17 says the explainer must never do this. No test covers mixed versions, and the plan says nothing about it.

findings.reason: quickstart.md is a plan-gate file, and flow.judged_blob compares non-tasks files by raw hash-object, so an older nio sees the Read first line as an edit; CT-9 and the plan say nothing on mixed versions and no test covers it.
findings.note: Accept as risk: single user, nio ships with the repo, so mixed versions are unlikely; if it happens the effort goes back to the plan jury once.

findings.title: It is not stated whether `finish` can be re-run after stopping halfway
quotes: deletes each SVG the old images line lists that sits in the explainer's own folder
running `npx -y MERMAID -i <temp .mmd> -o <out>` with `subprocess.run`
findings.fix: in CT-5, say that the explainer is written once, atomically (temp file plus `os.replace`), and that a listed file already gone is skipped silently. Give CT-3's `subprocess.run` a timeout that maps to `unreachable`. Add a test: an images line listing a missing `explainer-x.svg`; `finish` exits 0 and prints no `deleted:` line for it.

sources.situation: step 3 deletes orphan SVGs, then step 4 renders. Each render spawns `npx`, which can hang while fetching 382 MB and has no timeout. If `finish` is interrupted or killed during step 4, the explainer on disk still has its old images line and links, which point at files already deleted. The contract does not say whether the file is written once at the end or step by step. It also does not say whether step 3 treats an already-missing listed file as done or fails with `FileNotFoundError`. If it fails, every later `finish` fails. No test re-runs `finish` after a partial one.

findings.reason: CT-5 does not say whether the explainer is written once or stepwise, nor how step 3 treats an already-missing listed file, and CT-3 gives subprocess.run no timeout; no test re-runs finish after a partial one.
findings.note: finish writes once at the end, skips already-gone images, npx has a 120 s timeout; TC-45

findings.fix: have step 4 refuse, or add a numeric suffix to, a target name that another section in this run already uses, or that exists on disk without being listed in this explainer's images line. Use a separator that a slug cannot start with (for example `<stem>--<title slug>.svg`).

sources.situation: in `.nio/research/`, the stem `<date>-x-explainer` is a prefix of `<date>-x-explainer-2`. If the first file has a section titled `2 Overview`, its image is `<date>-x-explainer-2-overview.svg`, which is exactly the second file's `Overview` image. Rendering silently overwrites the other explainer's image, and a later orphan delete removes it. In the same way, two sections whose titles slug the same overwrite each other in one run.

findings.note: Images named <stem>--<title slug>.svg with -2, -3 on clash; TC-46
